positiveControls: authz.read.operator 200 proves the negative cases are not failing for an unrelated reason.
transport.corsPreflight.configuredOrigin 200 proves the rejection of a foreign origin is a policy decision, not a broken preflight path.
page.page11.query-root-projection 200 proves the page 11 include failure is specific to relation hydration.

limits: Only the dev API was exercised. Production was called once for GET /health and is covered by none of these results.

The dev container was NOT rebuilt or restarted, so the results describe the image the dev container was already running, not the current working tree. Another agent was changing source locally during the run.

No cross-realm token was obtained: the second realm on this authority is the administrative realm and getting a token from it would have required handling administrator credentials outside the provider container. The wrong-issuer case is therefore a self-signed token asserting a foreign issuer, which exercises the issuer check but not a genuine foreign authority's signature.
Mutating endpoints were called only with identities that lack the write authority, so the write path is proven to be refused but is not proven to work; nothing was mutated.
The matrix records the API's own response headers. Anything the edge adds (HSTS) was verified separately on the auth hostname and is not part of the API-path matrix.
Rate limiting was avoided, not tested: 41 paced requests stayed well inside the 120/60 s budget and no case returned 429. Behaviour under abuse is covered by ops/tests/load, not here.
Tenant VALUE enforcement is reported as a measured absence (SEC-2026-001). The suite cannot state the correct behaviour until the tenant claims model is decided.
Refresh-token handling, token revocation, introspection-endpoint behaviour and interactive login flows were not exercised: the deployment uses client_credentials service identities only.

The include-hydration check asserts that at least one returned row carries a non-empty value under each declared relation code. It never ran to completion here because the request was refused with 400.
This evidence is not signed.

Echoing a caller's own input back is not information the caller lacked; everything else in the body is compared verbatim, including type, title, code, detail template, status and media type.

findings.closedBy: run-2. The same identity now receives 404 on the distribution boundary, indistinguishable from an object that does not exist (oracle.distributionMasking, oracle.distributionMaskingCrossIdentity, oracle.signedDownloadMasking, oracle.signedDownloadMaskingCrossIdentity all PASS), and 403 problem+json with code tenant-access-denied on contract, page and id-addressed routes. The closure is load-bearing only because of the positive controls: an identity with the read role and the OWNING tenant, holding no cross-tenant authority, still receives 200 on the read endpoint (2 artifacts), on the signed-download issue endpoint, on both id-addressed routes and on page 8 introspection, capabilities and query.

findings.title: Token expiry carries a declared 60 s clock skew
findings.observed: A one-second token was accepted 5 s after expiry and refused 75 s after expiry.
findings.resolution: The skew is now explicit configuration, OIDC_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS (default 60, bounded 0..120), so the tolerated window is an approved, written number rather than an unexamined library default. The suite records the case as WITHIN_DECLARED_SKEW and keeps the +75 s case as the proof that expiry is enforced at all.

findings.title: Page 11 cannot hydrate either relation the approved revision declares
findings.observed: Unchanged in run-2. The capabilities document for page 11 revision 8 declares allowedIncludes INPUT_FOR_CARRIER and INPUT_RAW_LINEAGE. Requesting either, alone or together, returns HTTP 400 application/problem+json code contract-query-invalid, detail 'Only data-plane contract tables are queryable'. Without includes the same query returns 200 and 25 of 1760 rows.
findings.cause: In revision 8 the root dataset KIDS_STATISTICAL_INPUT is registered with storage_plane DATA, while both relation targets KIDS_STATISTICAL_CARRIER and KIDS_RAW_DOCUMENT are registered with storage_plane ACCESS; the physical query service refuses any non-DATA plane and the include path uses that same service.
findings.owner: the lead handles this as a contract migration; no source was changed by this session

findings.title: RFC 9457 and RFC 6750 on the error surface
findings.closedPart: The anonymous 401 is now application/problem+json with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, Cache-Control: no-store and nosniff, and the tenancy 403 is application/problem+json with code tenant-access-denied, no-store and nosniff. Both were asserted as header contracts in run-2 and PASS.
findings.remainingPart: see SEC-2026-007 and SEC-2026-008, which run-2 measured for the first time

findings.title: HSTS comes from the edge, not from the API, and the published API hostname points at production
findings.observed: Unchanged. The API emits Cache-Control, nosniff, CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN but no Strict-Transport-Security, because it is reached over plain HTTP inside the host. The edge adds HSTS. The edge's catch-all server block proxies /api/ to the PRODUCTION container, so no TLS hostname currently fronts the dev API.

findings.title: A 401 for a REJECTED bearer token carries no body at all, so it is not an RFC 9457 document
findings.observed: Twelve run-2 cases: every 401 caused by a token that was presented and refused (malformed, empty bearer value, tampered signature, unknown key, copied kid, alg=none, HS256 confusion x2, forged issuer, expired, not-yet-valid, blank tenant claim) returns a zero-byte body with NO Content-Type header. The RFC 6750 challenge is correct - WWW-Authenticate begins Bearer error="invalid_token" - and Cache-Control contains no-store and nosniff is present, but there is no problem document. The anonymous 401, which takes a different path, IS problem+json.
findings.consequence: The stated design 'refused bearer token 401 -> RFC 9457 problem+json' holds only for the no-credential path. A client cannot parse a uniform error document across the two 401 paths.
findings.secondaryObservation: The challenge also carries error_description text produced by the token decoder, for example 'An error occurred while attempting to decode the Jwt: Malformed token'. It leaks no secret and no data, but it describes an internal component to an unauthenticated caller.
findings.verdictUsed: FAIL_RESPONSE_CONTRACT (the status is correct; the declared response surface is not)

findings.title: A 403 for a MISSING AUTHORITY is still the legacy JSON shape and carries no insufficient_scope challenge
findings.observed: Five run-2 cases: a 403 caused by a missing authority (no role at all on the read, mutating and id-addressed routes; the cross-tenant reference identity on the administrative endpoint) returns Content-Type: application/json with a {timestamp,status,error,message,path,correlationId} body and NO WWW-Authenticate header. Cache-Control contains no-store and nosniff is present.
findings.contrast: The TENANCY 403 on the same routes is correct: application/problem+json, code tenant-access-denied, no-store, nosniff. Only the missing-authority branch was not migrated.
findings.consequence: The stated design '403 missing authority -> Bearer error="insufficient_scope"' is not met.

findings.title: problem+json responses declare charset=ISO-8859-1
findings.observed: The anonymous 401 and the 404/403 problem documents are served as application/problem+json;charset=ISO-8859-1. RFC 9457 documents are JSON and therefore UTF-8; a non-ASCII detail would be mis-encoded for a client that honours the declared charset.
findings.note: No non-ASCII detail text was produced by any case in either run, so no mis-encoding was observed.
